name: Bodyweight Squat
notes: Keep a neutral spine throughout. Stop if you feel knee or lower back pain.
description: A foundational lower-body movement that builds strength in your legs and glutes. One of the most effective exercises for beginners.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
Keep your chest up and core braced throughout the movement.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering toward the floor.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor, or as far as comfortable.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Reverse Lunge
notes: Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright. Avoid letting your front knee cave inward.
description: A single-leg exercise that targets the quads and glutes while improving balance and coordination.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Step one foot backward, lowering your back knee toward the floor.
Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Alternate legs each rep, or complete all reps on one side first.

name: Romanian Deadlift
notes: Keep your back flat throughout. Do not round your spine. Lower only as far as your hamstring flexibility allows.
description: A hip-hinge movement that stretches and strengthens the hamstrings and builds posterior chain strength.
instructions: Stand holding a pair of dumbbells in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at your hips, pushing them backward as you lower the weights along your legs.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and your back flat throughout.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, typically mid-shin level.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.

name: Glute Bridge
notes: Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top. Avoid overextending your lower back.
description: A floor exercise that isolates and activates the glutes with no equipment needed. Great for beginners.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your arms at your sides with palms facing down.
Press through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold for one to two seconds at the top.
Slowly lower your hips back to the floor and repeat.

name: Bicep Curl
notes: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides. Avoid swinging your torso to generate momentum.
description: The classic arm exercise for building bicep strength and size using dumbbells.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your elbows pinned close to your torso and palms facing forward.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders, squeezing the biceps at the top.
Avoid swinging your torso or using momentum.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Tricep Dip
notes: Keep your hips close to the chair and your shoulders down. Do not lock your elbows at the top.
description: A bodyweight exercise targeting the triceps using a chair or bench for support.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair with hands gripping the seat beside your hips.
Slide your hips off the seat, supporting your weight on your hands.
Keep your legs extended or bend them to 90 degrees for an easier variation.
Bend your elbows to lower your body toward the floor until elbows reach 90 degrees.
Press back up to the starting position, fully extending your arms.
Repeat without letting your hips rest on the floor between reps.

name: Hammer Curl
notes: Maintain a neutral (palms-facing-in) grip throughout. Do not rotate your wrists at the top.
description: A curl variation with a neutral grip that targets the biceps and brachialis for fuller arm development.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Keep your upper arms stationary and elbows close to your torso.
Curl the weights upward, maintaining the neutral palm-in grip throughout.
Squeeze at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower back to the starting position.
Alternate arms or curl both simultaneously.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
notes: Keep your upper arms close to your head and avoid flaring your elbows outward.
description: A dumbbell exercise that isolates the long head of the tricep through a full range of motion.
instructions: Stand or sit and hold one dumbbell with both hands directly overhead.
Keep your upper arms close to your head and elbows pointing forward.
Slowly lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Lower until your forearms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Press the dumbbell back overhead, fully extending your elbows.
Keep your core braced to avoid arching your lower back.

name: Push-Up
notes: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. Do not let your hips sag or pike upward.
description: A classic bodyweight exercise that builds chest, shoulder, and tricep strength simultaneously.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels — do not let your hips sag.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows at about a 45-degree angle.
Stop just before your chest touches the floor.
Press through your palms to return to the starting position.
For an easier variation, perform the movement from your knees.

name: Incline Push-Up
notes: The higher the surface, the easier the movement. Use this as a progression toward standard push-ups.
description: An elevated push-up variation that reduces load and targets the lower chest — great for beginners.
instructions: Place your hands on a raised surface such as a bench, chair, or step.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight diagonal line.
Lower your chest toward the surface by bending your elbows.
Keep your core tight and hips level throughout.
Press back up to the starting position.
The higher the surface, the easier the movement.

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
notes: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout. Avoid lowering your arms below chest level.
description: An isolation exercise that stretches and strengthens the chest through a wide arc of motion.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Slowly lower your arms out to the sides in an arc, feeling a stretch across your chest.
Lower until your hands are roughly level with your chest.
Reverse the arc, squeezing your chest muscles as you bring the weights back together.
Avoid locking your elbows or using momentum.

name: Diamond Push-Up
notes: This variation is harder than a standard push-up. Scale by performing from your knees if needed.
description: A narrow-grip push-up variation that shifts focus to the inner chest and triceps.
instructions: Place your hands close together under your sternum, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.
Extend your body into a straight plank position.
Lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Stop just before your chest touches the floor.
Press back up to the starting position.
Perform from your knees to reduce difficulty.

name: Bent-Over Row
muscle_groups_addressed: Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Rear Deltoids, Biceps
notes: Keep your back flat — do not round your spine. Drive your elbows behind you rather than flaring them out.
description: A compound pulling exercise that builds thickness in the mid-back and improves posture.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees slightly bent and your back flat — do not round your spine.
Let the dumbbells hang directly below your shoulders.
Pull the weights up toward your lower ribcage, driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Slowly lower back to the starting position and repeat.

name: Superman Hold
notes: Keep your neck neutral — do not look up. Squeeze your glutes at the top of the movement.
description: A floor exercise that strengthens the lower back and posterior chain with no equipment needed.
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your neck neutral — do not look up.
Hold the top position for two to three seconds.
Slowly lower back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Resistance Band Row
notes: Anchor the band securely. Keep your core engaged and avoid leaning back excessively.
description: A resistance band row that targets the lats and upper back — ideal for beginners without gym access.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at waist height around a door frame or sturdy post.
Hold one end of the band in each hand and step back until there is tension.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Pull both ends of the band toward your lower ribcage, driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position.

name: Reverse Dumbbell Fly
notes: Use lighter weights than you think you need. The movement is small — focus on squeezing your shoulder blades.
description: An isolation exercise for the rear deltoids and upper back that corrects postural imbalances.
instructions: Hold a light dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips about 45 degrees.
Let the dumbbells hang below your chest with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise both arms out to the sides in a wide arc until they are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.
Keep the movement controlled — avoid using momentum.

name: Plank
muscle_groups_addressed: Transverse Abdominis, Rectus Abdominis, Glutes, Shoulders
notes: Do not let your hips sag or rise. Breathe steadily throughout. Drop to your knees to reduce difficulty.
description: An isometric core exercise that builds endurance and stability throughout the entire midsection.
instructions: Start in a forearm plank position with elbows directly below your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core, glutes, and quads — do not let your hips sag or rise.
Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor just ahead of your hands.
Hold for the target duration, breathing steadily throughout.
To reduce difficulty, drop to your knees while maintaining a straight line from head to knees.

name: Crunch
notes: Do not pull on your neck. Press your lower back into the floor before initiating the movement.
description: A foundational abdominal exercise that isolates the rectus abdominis (the six-pack muscles).
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your hands lightly behind your head — do not pull on your neck.
Press your lower back into the floor and engage your core.
Curl your shoulders up off the floor using your abdominals.
Hold for a moment at the top, then slowly lower back down.
Exhale as you crunch up; inhale as you lower.

name: Russian Twist
notes: Keep your spine long and avoid rounding your lower back. Add a light weight to increase difficulty.
description: A rotational core exercise that targets the obliques and builds rotational strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet elevated slightly off the ground.
Lean back slightly to engage your core, keeping your spine long.
Clasp your hands together or hold a light weight in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to the right, then to the left — that is one rep.
Keep the movement controlled and your core engaged throughout.
Add a heavier weight to increase difficulty.

name: Mountain Climbers
notes: Keep your hips level — do not let them bounce. Slow the movement down for a more controlled core challenge.
description: A dynamic full-body movement that combines core stability with cardiovascular effort.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with arms straight and hands below your shoulders.
Keep your hips level and your body in a straight line.
Drive your right knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs.
Alternate legs as quickly as you can while maintaining plank form.
Keep your core tight throughout — do not let your hips bounce.
Slow the movement down for a more controlled core challenge.

name: Overhead Press
muscle_groups_addressed: Anterior Deltoids, Medial Deltoids, Triceps, Upper Trapezius
notes: Brace your core to protect your lower back. Do not lock your elbows at the top of the press.
description: A pressing movement that builds overall shoulder strength and stability using dumbbells.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back.
Press the weights directly overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Do not lock your elbows at the top.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

name: Lateral Raise
notes: Use lighter weights than you think — form matters more than load. Lead with your elbows, not your wrists.
description: An isolation exercise that targets the medial (side) deltoid for broader-looking shoulders.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Raise both arms out to your sides until they are parallel to the floor.
Lead with your elbows, not your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top, then slowly lower back to your sides.
Use lighter weights than you think you need — form matters more than load here.

name: Front Raise
notes: Avoid shrugging your shoulders at the top. Keep your core tight to prevent leaning back.
description: A shoulder isolation exercise that targets the front (anterior) deltoid.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Keep your arms nearly straight with a soft bend at the elbows.
Raise one or both arms forward to shoulder height, palms facing down.
Pause briefly at the top.
Slowly lower back to the starting position.
Alternate arms or raise both simultaneously.

name: Arnold Press
notes: Move slowly through the rotation. Do not rush the palm rotation — it is what makes this exercise effective.
description: A rotating dumbbell press that works all three heads of the deltoid through a unique range of motion.
instructions: Sit holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing toward you, as if finishing a curl.
As you press the weights upward, rotate your palms to face forward.
Fully extend your arms overhead at the top of the movement.
As you lower the weights, rotate your palms back to face you.
Return to the starting position and repeat.
Move slowly and with control through the full rotation.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
notes: Keep your front shin as vertical as possible and your torso upright. Complete all reps on one leg before switching.
description: A rear-foot-elevated single-leg squat that maximally loads the front leg, building unilateral strength and correcting imbalances.
instructions: Stand about two feet in front of a bench or chair and place one foot on top of it behind you.
Keep your front foot flat on the floor and your torso upright.
Lower your hips toward the floor by bending your front knee.
Descend until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Complete all reps on one leg before switching sides.

name: Jump Squat
notes: Land softly with bent knees to protect your joints. Avoid this exercise if you have knee or ankle issues.
description: An explosive plyometric squat that builds lower-body power and trains fast-twitch muscle fibers.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides.
Lower into a squat, pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Explode upward as powerfully as possible, leaving the ground entirely.
Swing your arms overhead to help generate height.
Land softly through your toes, then midfoot, then heels with knees bent.
Absorb the landing and immediately flow into the next rep.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
notes: Keep your hips square to the floor — do not let the non-working hip rotate open. A slight knee bend on the standing leg is fine.
description: A single-leg hip hinge that isolates each hamstring and glute while challenging balance and core stability.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with feet hip-width apart.
Shift your weight onto one leg and hinge forward at the hip.
Extend the non-working leg directly behind you as a counterbalance.
Keep your back flat and hips square to the floor throughout.
Lower the weights until you feel a strong stretch in the standing-leg hamstring.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing, then repeat on the other leg.

name: Zottman Curl
notes: Move slowly on the lowering phase — the eccentric overload on the forearms is the point of this exercise.
description: A curl variation that trains the biceps on the way up and the forearm extensors on the way down for complete arm development.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing forward.
Curl the weights up to shoulder height as in a standard bicep curl.
At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face downward.
Slowly lower the weights with palms down, taking 3–4 seconds.
At the bottom, rotate back to the starting supinated position.
Repeat, keeping the entire movement slow and controlled.

name: Skull Crusher
notes: Keep your upper arms perpendicular to the floor and stationary throughout. Use lighter weight until you are confident in your form.
description: A lying tricep extension that applies concentrated load to all three heads of the tricep for maximum development.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench or the floor holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest.
Position your upper arms perpendicular to the floor and keep them stationary throughout.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells toward the sides of your head.
Stop when your forearms are parallel to the floor or slightly past.
Press back up by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight.
Repeat without letting your upper arms drift forward or backward.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
notes: Keep your upper arms pinned to the incline pad throughout. Avoid swinging or using momentum.
description: A curl performed on an incline bench that fully elongates the bicep at the start for a deeper stretch and stronger peak contraction.
instructions: Set a bench to a 45-degree incline and sit back against it holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down at your sides, fully extended.
Curl both weights simultaneously, keeping your upper arms pinned to the pad.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the weights back to the fully extended starting position.
Do not swing your torso or use momentum to initiate the curl.

name: Archer Push-Up
notes: Keep the extended arm actively pushing into the floor even though it stays straight. This is a significant strength challenge.
description: A unilateral push-up variation that shifts nearly all load to one arm at a time, bridging the gap toward a one-arm push-up.
instructions: Start in a wide push-up position with hands spaced about twice shoulder-width apart.
Lower toward one hand by bending only that arm's elbow while keeping the other arm straight.
Press firmly into the floor with the extended arm for support.
Descend until your chest is close to the floor on the bending-arm side.
Push back up to the starting position.
Alternate sides each rep or complete all reps on one side first.

name: Plyometric Push-Up
notes: Land with softly bent elbows to absorb impact. Do not attempt this if you cannot complete 15 controlled standard push-ups.
description: An explosive push-up where you press hard enough for your hands to leave the floor, building upper-body power.
instructions: Start in a standard push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower your chest to the floor with control.
Press as explosively as possible so your hands leave the floor.
Clap your hands together if possible, then land with softly bent elbows.
Absorb the landing and immediately lower into the next rep.
Maintain a tight plank position throughout — do not let your hips sag.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
muscle_groups_addressed: Chest, Latissimus Dorsi, Serratus Anterior, Triceps
notes: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout. Brace your core to prevent excessive lower back arch at the bottom.
description: A lying pullover that stretches and strengthens both the chest and lats through an extreme range of motion.
instructions: Lie perpendicular across a bench with your upper back and shoulders supported.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands directly above your chest, arms slightly bent.
Brace your core and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head toward the floor.
Lower until your upper arms are roughly in line with your torso.
Reverse the arc and pull the weight back to the starting position above your chest.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled — avoid dropping into the stretch.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
muscle_groups_addressed: Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Rear Deltoids, Biceps
notes: Drive your elbow straight back rather than flaring it outward. Allow a small amount of shoulder rotation at the top to maximize lat engagement.
description: A unilateral row that allows heavier loading and greater range of motion than a bilateral bent-over row.
instructions: Place your non-working hand and same-side knee on a bench for support.
Hold a dumbbell in the working hand and let it hang straight down.
Keep your back flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Row the dumbbell up toward your hip, driving your elbow straight behind you.
Squeeze your lat and upper back at the top.
Lower the weight with control until your arm is fully extended, then repeat.

name: Renegade Row
notes: Use hex dumbbells for stability. Keep your hips square to the floor — do not rotate your torso as you row.
description: A push-up position row that simultaneously challenges upper-back strength and anti-rotational core stability.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with each hand gripping a dumbbell on the floor.
Walk your feet slightly wider than hip-width to create a stable base.
Brace your core and keep your hips square to the floor.
Row one dumbbell up toward your hip while balancing on the other arm.
Lower it back to the floor with control, then row the other side.
Avoid rotating your torso or letting your hips shift as you row.

name: Good Morning
muscle_groups_addressed: Hamstrings, Glutes, Lower Back, Spinal Erectors
notes: Never round your lower back under load. Start without weight to learn the hinge pattern before adding resistance.
description: A hip-hinge movement that strengthens the spinal erectors and hamstrings, building a resilient posterior chain.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands clasped behind your head.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees throughout the movement.
Hinge forward at the hips, pushing them back as your torso descends.
Keep your spine neutral — do not allow your lower back to round.
Lower until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor or as far as flexibility allows.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing and squeeze your glutes at the top.

name: Hollow Body Hold
muscle_groups_addressed: Transverse Abdominis, Rectus Abdominis, Hip Flexors
notes: Press your lower back firmly into the floor throughout. If your back lifts off, raise your legs higher until contact is maintained.
description: A gymnastics-based isometric hold that creates full-body tension and serves as the foundation of advanced bodyweight training.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor — this is the critical cue.
Simultaneously lift your arms, shoulders, and legs off the floor.
Reach your arms back and extend your legs to about 30–45 degrees.
Hold the position while breathing steadily and keeping your lower back pressed down.
To make it easier, raise your legs higher or bend your knees toward your chest.

name: V-Up
notes: Keep your legs as straight as possible. If hamstring flexibility limits you, a slight knee bend is acceptable.
description: A dynamic core exercise that simultaneously raises your arms and legs to form a V-shape, training the full abdominal wall.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Simultaneously lift your arms and straight legs off the floor.
Reach your hands toward your feet, aiming to meet above your hips.
Hold the top position briefly, feeling your entire core engage.
Slowly lower your arms and legs back toward the floor without fully resting.
Maintain core tension throughout — do not let your lower back arch.

name: Dragon Flag
muscle_groups_addressed: Rectus Abdominis, Core, Hip Flexors, Spinal Erectors
notes: Only lower as far as you can while keeping your body rigid. Tuck your knees as a regression if needed.
description: A gymnastic core exercise that holds the entire body rigid in a cantilevered position, made famous by Bruce Lee.
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip the sides firmly behind your head for support.
Press your shoulders into the bench and lift your entire lower body straight up.
Keep your body in a perfectly rigid straight line from shoulders to feet.
Slowly lower your body toward horizontal, maintaining full rigidity.
Stop just before your lower back would contact the bench.
Drive back up to vertical using your core and repeat.

name: Pike Push-Up
muscle_groups_addressed: Anterior Deltoids, Medial Deltoids, Triceps, Upper Chest
notes: The more vertical your torso, the greater the shoulder demand. Elevate your feet on a bench to progress toward a handstand push-up.
description: A bodyweight overhead pressing movement that loads the shoulders far more than a standard push-up.
instructions: Start in a downward dog position with hips raised high and legs straight.
Position your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, fingers pointing forward.
Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands.
Keep your hips elevated — resist the urge to let them drop.
Press back up by extending your elbows until your arms are straight.
To increase difficulty, elevate your feet on a bench.

name: Single-Arm Overhead Press
muscle_groups_addressed: Anterior Deltoids, Medial Deltoids, Triceps, Core
notes: Brace your core hard to prevent lateral lean. Do not let your torso tilt away from the working arm.
description: A unilateral overhead press that challenges shoulder strength alongside core stability and anti-lateral-flexion.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in one hand at shoulder height, palm facing forward.
Brace your core and keep your torso upright — do not lean away from the weight.
Press the dumbbell directly overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Do not lock your elbow at the top.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to shoulder height.
Complete all reps on one arm before switching.

name: Bradford Press
muscle_groups_addressed: All Three Deltoid Heads, Trapezius, Triceps
notes: Use a very light weight — the continuous arc is far more taxing than a standard press. Avoid lowering behind the neck if you have shoulder impingement.
description: A continuous arc pressing drill that cycles dumbbells from chest to overhead to behind-the-neck, building shoulder endurance and mobility.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press the weights overhead, stopping just short of lockout.
Without pausing, continue the arc to lower the weights behind your head to upper-trap height.
Reverse direction by pressing back overhead and lowering to the front starting position.
That full cycle counts as one rep.
Keep the weight light and the movement smooth — avoid shrugging or rushing.
